# VeilPay Website Integration Guide

Everything an agent (or human) needs to plug the deployed VeilPay payment-intent
contract into a website.

## What The Contract Is

VeilPay is a privacy-preserving payment-intent protocol. A merchant publishes a
checkout request on-chain; a customer settles it by proving knowledge of a
payment secret inside a ZK circuit. The public ledger records **that** a
payment is verified and its amount, but never who paid.

Public ledger state (`ledger sequence`, `ledger intents: Map<Uint<64>, Intent>`):

```
Intent {
  merchantId       Bytes<32>   // H(merchantSecretKey) -- pseudonymous
  amount           Uint<128>   // requested amount
  expiresAt        Uint<64>    // intent-operations deadline (see below)
  status           IntentStatus // ACTIVE | PAID | REFUNDED | CANCELLED
  secretCommitment Bytes<32>   // H("veilpay:intent:", id, paymentSecret)
  paidAmount       Uint<128>
  refundedAmount   Uint<128>
}
```

Circuits:

| Circuit | Caller | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `createIntent(amount, expiresAt)` | merchant (proves knowledge of `merchantSecretKey`) | inserts a new ACTIVE intent, returns its id |
| `pay(intentId)` | anyone holding the intent's `paymentSecret` | marks PAID, records `paidAmount = amount` |
| `refund(intentId, refundAmount)` | merchant only | marks REFUNDED, records refunded amount |
| `cancel(intentId)` | merchant only | marks CANCELLED (unpaid intents only) |
| `isPaid(intentId)` | anyone (pure) | returns true when PAID or REFUNDED |

The payment secret is generated by the merchant when creating the intent and
handed to the customer out-of-band (checkout link, QR, chat). Paying proves
knowledge of it in-circuit; the payer's identity never touches public state.

**Expiry semantics.** Compact has no timestamp oracle, so `expiresAt` counts
intent-operations: the contract asserts `sequence <= expiresAt` at pay time,
where `sequence` increments on every create/pay/refund/cancel across the whole
contract. The CLI anchors `expiresAt = currentSequence + ttlOps` on creation.
Treat the TTL as a liveness bound, not a wall-clock deadline.

## Architecture

All contract interaction happens server-side. The frontend never holds keys.

```
Browser                Next.js / Node server                 Midnight Preprod
---------              ------------------------------        ----------------
checkout page  ----->  POST /api/create-intent  ----+
                            |  VeilPayAPI.createIntent  |  gateway: prove,
                            |  (merchant key server-side)|  balance, submit
                            v                           |---------------->
payment link/QR + secret
customer pays  ----->  POST /api/pay  -> VeilPayAPI.pay ---->
merchant dashboard  -> GET /api/status -> isPaid / ledger
```

The server talks to Preprod through the sponsored 1AM gateway
(`https://api-preprod.1am.xyz`), which removes every operational blocker of the
vanilla SDK path:

| Blocker (official path) | Gateway solution |
|---|---|
| Faucet unusable (Turnstile mints nothing) | `/balance-only` sponsors dust fees |
| Shielded sync replays entire zswap history | no wallet sync; keys derived directly from seed |
| Local proof server required | hosted `/check` + `/prove` |
| Node websocket required | `/rpc/midnight` JSON-RPC proxy (`author_submitExtrinsic`) |
| Public indexer unauthenticated / geo-blocked | authenticated indexer relay (session token injected locally) |
| SDK inclusion-watch never resolves (polls by identifier, submit returns extrinsic hash) | HTTP polling watches keyed by the Midnight tx hash from `/balance-only` |

All of that is implemented once in `cli/src/gateway-stack.ts` and exported as
`buildGatewayStack()`, which returns the exact provider object
`VeilPayAPI.deploy()` / `VeilPayAPI.join()` expect.

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/thirdbase1/veilpay.git
cd veilpay
npm install
```

You need a gateway session. Either run the CLI once (it authenticates with a
BIP-340 Schnorr signature and caches the token), or copy an existing session:

```
cli/.veilpay-state/gw_session.json    # {"token": "...", "address": "..."}
cli/.veilpay-state/contract-address   # 0x3046...
```

Never commit these. They are gitignored (`cli/.veilpay-state/`). The wallet
seed lives in `cli/.veilpay-state/wallet.seed`; in production, load it from a
secret manager instead and pass it as the `VEILPAY_SEED` env var.

## Server-Side Integration (Next.js App Router)

### Provider singleton

Create one provider stack per process and reuse it. Put this in
`lib/veilpay-server.ts`:

```ts
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { VeilPayAPI } from '../veilpay/api/src/index.js';
import { buildGatewayStack, ADDRESS_FILE } from '../veilpay/cli/src/gateway-stack.js';

let apiPromise: Promise<VeilPayAPI> | null = null;

export function veilpay(): Promise<VeilPayAPI> {
  if (!apiPromise) {
    apiPromise = (async () => {
      const logger = { info: (m: string) => console.log('[veilpay]', m) };
      const { providers, close } = await buildGatewayStack(logger);
      const address = process.env.VEILPAY_CONTRACT_ADDRESS
        ?? fs.readFileSync(ADDRESS_FILE, 'utf8').trim();
      const api = await VeilPayAPI.join(providers, address, logger);
      // keep `close` around for graceful shutdown if you need it
      return api;
    })().catch((e) => { apiPromise = null; throw e; });
  }
  return apiPromise;
}
```

### Merchant creates an intent

```ts
// app/api/create-intent/route.ts
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { veilpay } from '@/lib/veilpay-server';

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { amount } = await req.json();            // string or number
  const api = await veilpay();

  const state = await api.providers.publicDataProvider
    .queryContractState(api.deployedContractAddress);
  const { ledger } = await import('../veilpay/contract/src/managed/veilpay/contract/index.js');
  const seq = ledger(state.data).sequence;

  const paymentSecret = randomBytes(32);
  const id = await api.createIntent(BigInt(amount), seq + 50n, paymentSecret);

  // Return the secret ONCE over HTTPS; the customer needs it to pay.
  return Response.json({
    id: id.toString(),
    paymentSecret: Buffer.from(paymentSecret).toString('hex'),
  });
}
```

The id is deterministic (next sequence number), so no storage is required --
but persist the payment secret against your order if you need to re-issue the
checkout link.

### Customer pays

```ts
// app/api/pay/route.ts
import { veilpay } from '@/lib/veilpay-server';

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { id, paymentSecret } = await req.json();
  const api = await veilpay();
  await api.pay(BigInt(id), Buffer.from(paymentSecret, 'hex'));
  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

### Verify payment (no secrets involved)

```ts
// app/api/is-paid/route.ts
import { veilpay } from '@/lib/veilpay-server';

export async function GET(req: Request) {
  const id = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get('id') ?? '';
  const api = await veilpay();
  const paid = await api.isPaid(BigInt(id));
  return Response.json({ id, paid });
}
```

`isPaid` only reads public state through the indexer -- safe to call from any
page, including the customer's checkout status screen.

### Refund / cancel (merchant)

```ts
const api = await veilpay();
await api.refund(BigInt(id), BigInt(refundAmount)); // PAID intents only
await api.cancel(BigInt(id));                       // ACTIVE intents only
```

Both circuits prove the merchant identity in-circuit, so only the merchant key
holder can call them; the website just needs the merchant seed loaded.

## Full Lifecycle

```
            createIntent(amount, expiresAt)
                      |
                      v
                   [ACTIVE] ---- cancel (merchant) ----> [CANCELLED]
                      |
                pay (any secret holder, ZK-proven)
                      v
                    [PAID] ---- refund (merchant, any amount <= paid) ----> [REFUNDED]
```

Every transition is enforced by an assert inside the ZK circuit; off-chain
code cannot skip a rule because the network checks the proof.

Working example, run live on preprod from this repo:

```bash
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- status
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- create 2500 50
# -> { "id": "1", "paymentSecret": "4ed2..." }
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- pay 1 4ed2...
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- refund 1 1000
```

## Building And Testing

```bash
# unit tests (10) against the simulated ledger
npm --workspace contract run test

# typecheck everything
npm --workspace contract run typecheck
npm --workspace api run typecheck
npm --workspace cli run typecheck

# rebuild compiled artifacts (only needed if veilpay.compact changes)
npm --workspace contract run compact   # requires compactc or the CI artifact
```

`contract/src/managed/` is gitignored; CI compiles it fresh with
`midnightntwrk/setup-compact-action@v1` (compact 0.31.1) and uploads the
`veilpay-managed` artifact. Grab it from the latest green run if you do not
have a local compiler.

## Gotchas

- **Session expiry.** The gateway token is long-lived but not forever; if you
  start seeing 401/403 from the indexer or gateway, delete
  `cli/.veilpay-state/gw_session.json` and re-auth.
- **Dust sync staleness.** `/balance-only` occasionally returns
  `503 WALLETS_UNAVAILABLE / DUST_SYNC_STALE`. The stack retries with the
  server's `retryAfterMs` hint (up to 10 attempts); wait and retry if exhausted.
- **Transient network drops.** Every watch/query is HTTP polling with
  retries, but a long local outage can still surface as `fetch failed` during
  `join`. Just rerun the command.
- **expiresAt is not a date.** It is an operation counter across the whole
  contract. The CLI anchors it to `currentSequence + ttlOps`.
- **Intent ids are dense.** Next id = `sequence + 1`; the API pre-seeds the
  payment secret for the predicted id before proving `createIntent`.
- **Secrets are one-shot.** A paid intent cannot be paid again (`status` must
  be ACTIVE). Generate a fresh secret per intent.
- **Merchant identity is derived, not stored.** `merchantId = H(sk)`. The same
  seed always maps to the same merchant id; rotating the seed rotates identity.

## Reference Commands

```bash
# deploy a NEW contract (writes cli/.veilpay-state/contract-address)
npm --workspace cli run preprod-gateway

# lifecycle against the deployed contract
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- status
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- create <amount> [ttlOps]
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- pay <id> <secretHex>
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- refund <id> <amount>
npm --workspace cli run preprod-tx -- cancel <id>

# read-only live check
node --experimental-specifier-resolution=node scripts/verify-live.mjs
```
